name: Bynder
tagline: Enterprise digital asset management: one branded library for logos, photos, video and the approval workflow around them.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified. Bynder is quote-based enterprise pricing with no public list price.

verdictSummary: The part of Bynder a single person or a two-person brand team actually touches is a searchable, tagged, thumbnailed file library with shareable links, and that is a weekend build. An agent can give you drag-and-drop ingest, auto thumbnails, EXIF and metadata extraction, tag and collection filters, and expiring share URLs without much drama. What does not survive the port is everything that exists because twelve departments and three agencies share the library: approval chains, usage rights expiry, brand guideline portals, role-based permissions, SSO, audit trails, and the plugin shelf that pushes assets straight into Adobe, Figma, Sitecore and whatever CMS marketing is on. Rendition pipelines (auto crops, format variants, a real CDN in front of them) are technically doable but tedious and you will be paying for egress yourself. Build it if you are the only librarian; do not build it if the actual product being bought is a system of record other companies trust.
coreLoopDIY: A local web app where you drop files in, it generates thumbnails and pulls metadata, then you tag, collect, search and hand out expiring share links.
requirements: Node 20+ and a machine to run it on
Disk space, and a plan for backups you will not actually make
A reverse proxy plus TLS if you want share links to work off your laptop
whatYouLose: Approval workflows, versioning with reviewers, and asset usage rights with expiry dates
Granular permissions, SSO and audit logs that satisfy a security review
Native plugins and connectors into Adobe apps, Figma, CMSes and ad platforms
Automatic renditions and a global CDN, so big video and print files will feel slow
Brand guideline portals and public-facing brand hubs that clients can be pointed at
moatNotes: Once five years of campaign assets and their metadata live inside a DAM, the migration cost is the product.
whyPeopleStillPay: Nobody buys a DAM because storing files is hard. They buy it because a marketing org needs one place where the approved logo lives, where legal can see when a model release expires, where an agency can be given access to exactly one folder, and where the CMS pulls the current hero image without anyone emailing a zip. That is coordination and accountability infrastructure, not a file browser, and the price tag is mostly indemnity against someone shipping the old logo. A personal build covers the storage and search; it cannot cover the part where other people are also expected to behave.
notes: Great solo asset library, lousy system of record. The moat is not the files, it is the approval trail and the connectors other teams already depend on.
prompt:
Build a self-hosted personal digital asset library called "Shelf". Single user, runs on my machine, no accounts, no cloud, no telemetry.

Stack, non-negotiable: Next.js 15 (App Router, TypeScript), SQLite via better-sqlite3, sharp for image processing, fluent-ffmpeg shelling out to a system ffmpeg for video posters, Tailwind for styling. No ORM, write plain SQL. No external services.

Storage: originals go to ./data/originals/{hash[0:2]}/{hash}.{ext}, derivatives to ./data/thumbs. Dedupe on sha256. SQLite file at ./data/shelf.db. Everything under ./data is gitignored.

Features, in scope:
- Drag-and-drop upload page, multi-file, with progress. Accept images, video, PDF, audio, zip.
- On ingest: hash, store, read EXIF/IPTC with exifr for images, probe duration and dimensions for video/audio, generate 320px and 1200px webp thumbs for images, a poster frame at 1s for video, and a first-page render for PDF via pdfjs-dist.
- Asset grid with infinite scroll, keyboard navigation, and a detail drawer showing all extracted metadata.
- Tags (many-to-many), plus freeform collections. Bulk tag and bulk collect from multi-select in the grid.
- Full text search across filename, tags, notes and extracted metadata using SQLite FTS5.
- Filters: type, tag, collection, date range, orientation.
- Share links: create a token per asset or per collection with an optional expiry timestamp. A /s/{token} route serves a read-only gallery and direct downloads. Expired or revoked tokens 404.
- Download menu per image offering original, 2048px, 1024px, and a square 512 crop, generated on demand and cached in ./data/thumbs.
- A /api/assets JSON endpoint so I can script against it.

Out of scope, do not build: user accounts, roles, approval workflows, comments, versioning, SSO, any third-party integration, any analytics.

Put the share-link signing secret in .env as SHELF_SECRET and read it with a startup check that fails loudly if missing. Ship a README with setup, the ffmpeg prerequisite, and a one-command `npm run dev`. Include a `npm run reindex` script that rebuilds thumbs and FTS from the originals on disk, so the database is disposable.
